full_judgment:
2. Plaintiff filed the suit for declaration of title to and confirmation of possession in the suit land. According to the plaintiff their father Osman Mondal was owner of /8/- annas of the tenancy recorded in khatian No. 736 of  mouza Sadipur. He transferred the suit land along with other last by executing pasta Ext. 1 dated 17.3.56 in favour defendant Nos. 1 and 3 by way of security for loan of Rs.150/. Plaintiffs Inherited the land from their father and repaid the consideration on 21.7.62. They got back the land but the defendants did not return the patta. During the Rent-roll operation the disputed property was recorded in the name of defendant No. 1. Defendant No. 1 threes tend plaintiff to dispossess the property Chaitra, 1372 B S. In the above circumstances the plaintiff filed the suit. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit on the ground that Osman Mondal learned out the disputed land to defendant No. by Patta Ext. 1 dated 17.1.56 and delivered, possession to them. They paid rent to Osman Mondal and later on to the Government Acquired Estate on receipt of dakhilad, They noticed the allegation of the plaintiffs. 

 4. The learned Munsif considered the case on merit and held that the lease by Ext. 1 is null and void under the provision of section 75(A) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as it was made after 16.12.55 Nevertheless the trial Court found that defendants paid rent to the Government and Governments recognised defendants as tenants and that names of the defendants have been records in the Rent roll. In this view of the matter the trial Court held that plaintiff is not called to any relief in the suit. Therefore, he dismissed the suit. 

 7. Mr. Mahbubur Rahman the learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that the judgment of the lower appellate Court Is not a judgment of proper reversal. In view of the fact that the learned lower appellate Court did not controvert the finding and decision of the trial Court to the effect that defendants were recognised as tenants by the Government, that defendants pale rent to the Government and received dakhilas and the Rent-roll was also prepared by the Government in their names. He, therefore, submits that defendants are entitled to get the disputed lard. The learned Advocate submits that Judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court are liable to be set aside. 

 8. It is correct that lower appellate Court did not discuss and controvert the findings and decision of the trial Court with regard to the facts that defendants paid rent to the Government and got dakhilas, their Rent-roll was prepared by the Government in the names of the defendants. The appellate Court also did not say anything whether defendants were recognised as tenants by the Government. 

 9. Both the Courts concurrently found that Ext. 1, the patta, is null and void and as such defendants cannot have any right and title and interest in the disputed property. The patta was executed on 17.3.56 and on that date the provision of law under section 75A was; 

 10. The next question is that defendants paid rent to the Government and obtained dakhilas and defendant's names was also recorded In the R.S. Khatian, Government did not forfeit the disputed land as the sub-lease was prior to 29.9.56 The question of recognition of the defendant by the Government as tenants In the circumstances does not arise. This being the position although there is no discussion and findings by the appellate Court about this aspect of the case It cannot be said that judgment of the appellate Court suffers from any Illegality and that decision is contrary to law and procedure. I, therefore, do not find anything to interfere with the Judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate Court.
